## Verdict: ACCEPT-WITH-CONDITIONS — PR #6937, head `6808939d9`, clause ② review of the `ComponentConfig` narrowing

One condition, and it is a two-line frontmatter edit plus one sentence; everything else was re-derived independently and reproduced exactly. Every reading below is my own measurement on fresh builds of base `40c479af2` (the true merge-base; the stated base `b03ba3ad` is main's tip, one PR ahead) and head `6808939d9`, probes compiled against the emitted `.d.ts` of both packages only, exit codes captured before any pipe.

### 1. Routing — clause ② was correctly applied; the PM is right

The narrowing is real and published: my cross-tree probe on the two emitted core surfaces reads the set difference of keys on base-core's `ComponentConfig` minus head-core's as exactly `tier | namespace | skipFallback | labelling | deprecated`, and nothing in the other direction. A consumer hits it the ordinary way: on head, `c.tier` off `ComponentConfig` imported from `@object-ui/core` gives — the compiler's own line — `error TS2339: Property 'tier' does not exist on type 'ComponentConfig[any]'`, and the literal form gives `error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'tier' does not exist in type 'ComponentConfig[any]'`; both spellings compile green on base (hot control, same instrument, same pass). Out-of-repo consumers are unmeasurable, so review was owed. Routing correct; no lighter path.

But the review's answer is that the narrowing should land, because it is **constitutive of the fix, not collateral**. The precise loser class: a consumer who (i) named `ComponentConfig` from `@object-ui/core` rather than from `@object-ui/types`, AND (ii) read or wrote one of the five registry-only keys against that annotation. Getter-fed consumers lose nothing — all three getters return `RegistryComponentConfig`, which I measured type-identical to the old core declaration (key set equal against the base tree's own emitted type, per-key member equality, parameterised slot equal). In-repo the loser class is empty: my own census, multi-line-import aware, finds 0 import clauses naming bare `ComponentConfig` from `@object-ui/core` across packages/apps/examples/e2e, with the control hot in the same pass (`ComponentRegistry` 388 import clauses, `ComponentMeta` 5); 0 module augmentations of `@object-ui/types`. The break is compile-loud with a mechanical one-line fix (import `RegistryComponentConfig`, or the same name from `@object-ui/types`), and the runtime surface is untouched.

### 2. No deprecation shim exists inside the repo's own ruling set — so none is owed

I checked every shape a shim could take. A derived local declaration in core (direction (a)) keeps a second authority — the gate's own doc: a declaration is an authority, and *"⛔ A deliberate re-export is NOT an authority"* — so the mandated `KNOWN_COLLISIONS` deletion is undeliverable that way. An aliasing re-export (`RegistryComponentConfig as ComponentConfig`) is **also** counted as an authority (gate doc and its own spelling-table test) and would additionally make the two published names *genuinely different types again*, which is the #4580 defect itself. A temporal window (keep the old declaration deprecated for one release) keeps the defect standing and the baseline row owed. The #5671 `ComponentInput` precedent — the same re-export disposition — shipped with no window. Landing as-is is right on all four axes; no maintainer ruling is needed, because the maintainer's standing policy already decides both the disposition (#4580 family ruling) and the grading (next section).

### 3. The ghost is real, and the new pin bites — both verified by measurement

**Ghost, measured on base:** on the diverged pair read from the emitted `.d.ts`, both directions of assignability typed `true` in my probe while the same program read the key-set difference as the five keys and `error TS2315: Type 'ComponentConfig' is not generic` (its own line) on the types side. Exit 0 on the pass-probe, so mutual assignability was green on two genuinely different types — an assignability pin would have been born green and stayed green. The dev's decision to build the pin on key sets + source identity and demote assignability to a labelled control is correct.

**Bite, by mutating the fact:** in the head worktree I replaced the re-export line in `Registry.ts` with the old local declaration — prediction written before the run: pin red on both source-identity assertions, gate red in the FRESH direction. Mutation proven on disk (anchored count 1 to 0, `git hash-object` `944093f2b` to `98547925d`), no rebuild involved (both instruments are source scans — a measured property of the gate, confirmed). Observed exactly the prediction: `Tests 3 failed | 18 passed (21)` — `× re-exports the canonical declaration and names the extension`, `× declares no ComponentConfig of its own`, and the gate's `ComponentConfig — a NEW colliding name`. Restore proven both ways under trap EXIT INT TERM with absolute paths: hash back to the HEAD blob, anchored count back to 1, `git diff HEAD` 0 lines. Enforcement of the type-level pins is real, not vitest theater: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` exit 0 shows the pin file in the program (1), reading `packages/types/dist/base.d.ts` (1) and types src (0).

### 4. Direction (a)'s exclusion holds on the tree

`Registry.ts:260` on head still carries the (a)-shaped `ComponentMeta` declaration PR #6297 landed, and `KNOWN_COLLISIONS` line 374 still carries its row — one line below the comment block where the `ComponentConfig` row was removed. The dev's counterexample is live and load-bearing, and it is why triage's fallback was never actually available for this card's mandated outcome.

### 5. Re-export shape — correct, and the only legal one

`export type` on the re-export is required, not stylistic: `tsconfig.base.json` sets `isolatedModules: true`, under which a value-form re-export of a type-only name is a compile error, and the emitted `Registry.js` would otherwise carry a runtime re-export of a binding `@object-ui/types` never emits. What core publishes is proven empirically: my head probe imports `ComponentConfig` from core's emitted `dist/index.d.ts` (through the `export *` chain) and instantiates it — generic, identical to types' (mutual Exact true, key diffs never both ways, bare slot still `any`, `ComponentRenderer` still the identity). And the rehoming was forced, not decorative: `namespace` is in the extras-only key set, so a bare re-export as the entry type would have broken `getNamespaceComponents`' filter in core's own build.

### 6. THE CONDITION — regrade the changeset from patch/patch to minor

The grade contradicts the repo's written policy and every family precedent. AGENTS.md §版本号策略: "objectui 自身的破坏性变更也标 `minor`(在正文里写清 breaking 语义即可)", restated in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s own header: *"objectui's own breaking changes ship as minor with the break spelled out in the changeset body."* Precedents: PR #5671 — the identical re-export disposition — graded **minor** on both packages; PR #6297 graded **minor** on core; PR #6936 (the sibling this review is consistency-paired with) graded **minor** on types. This PR removes five keys from a published type name on core (breaking for the class in §1) and adds a type parameter plus a new exported name on both — additive capability. `patch` is wrong on both entries by the repo's own convention; the fixed-group mechanics make the released version identical either way, but the changeset is the release-notes input and a narrowing filed as patch mis-signals there.

**Condition:** in `.changeset/6298-componentconfig-one-authority.md`, change both `patch` entries to `minor`, and add one sentence to the body naming the breaking class plainly, e.g.: "Breaking for consumers importing `ComponentConfig` from `@object-ui/core` and touching a registry-only key on it — switch that annotation to `RegistryComponentConfig`." The body's existing content is accurate and stays.

Nothing else blocks. With the regrade in, this lands as-is: no shim, no deprecation window, no maintainer escalation.
